title: valid-verbs-standard-cli-vocabulary
owner: CC owns the mechanism. Akien owns the verb list and their semantics (get=JSON, show=human-readable, etc.).
intention: A declared vocabulary of standard CLI verbs (get, show, list, ...) that every device implements through its shim, with validation of new commands against the vocabulary and standard shortcuts that compose into the full form.
why: Akien, 2026-08-27: 'we need a list of common verbs new things can't step on. like get should return whatever is asked for, prolly in json format. and show should prolly return the same thing, but formatted for humans, like in chat.' Without a vocabulary, cairn trouble get and cairn tester get could mean different things. Claude is the user — one mental model for all devices.
traces_to: Law 1 — a settled verb vocabulary means new commands don't re-derive what 'get' or 'show' means.
Law 4 — validation against the vocabulary is enforcement by physics (the shim refuses a colliding verb), not policy.
The complexity axis — the root shim class is the base that devices extend; common verbs are the base vocabulary.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: the root shim declares verbs, a device inherits them, get returns JSON, show returns human-readable, a colliding verb is refused. FEEDS BACK: a red names which verb or device failed.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when (1) the root shim class declares standard verbs with semantics, (2) devices inherit common handlers, (3) collisions are refused, (4) cairn device get thing works uniformly. WRONG INTENT if the vocabulary is prose, if devices must opt in, or if standard verbs don't compose.
falsifier.horizon: Moderate to large — touches the root shim class, device shims, and cairn command dispatch.

children: b41b0c0fff0e hot-and-the-root-verbs-resolve-in-the-shim (cast 2026-09-06: the resolver this vocabulary demands)

questions.a: ADDRESSING vs ACTION: the-cli-reaches-any-device is the addressing layer (making every device reachable). This is the action layer (what you can DO once you reach a device). They compose.

STANDARD vs DEVICE-SPECIFIC: the standard set is SMALL and reserved (get, show, list). Device-specific verbs are OPEN. The vocabulary governs standard verbs; device verbs are unconstrained beyond not colliding.
LONG FORM vs SHORTCUT: 'cairn device get thing' is the standard; 'cairnhelp' is a shortcut. The vocabulary is the source; shortcuts are views.

how.vocabulary: A data structure in the root shim class mapping verb names to their semantics. RULED 2026-09-06 (Akien, verbatim on the note of that date): the root set is exactly list, show, get, stop, start, settings. get returns JSON, show renders human-readable, list enumerates. `status` is a root view: list/show/get status carry the same content the web STATUS pane carries (shim.active_page: introspect()['intention'] + ['state']). `settings` carries the same content as the web SETTINGS pane (introspect()['settings']) and answers 'No settings' when the device declares none. start/stop act on the device instance's process (a device is its own process in the rack).
how.inheritance: The root shim class implements common verb handlers (get pid, get uptime, list verbs). Devices inherit and can extend with device-specific verbs.
how.dispatch: cairn <device> <verb> <args> → device shim's verb handler. Extends the COMPOSING_DOOR pattern (commit a9e1943).
how.validation: A verb that collides with a standard one is refused at registration time (Law 4).
how.composability: cairnhelp = cairn cairn show help. The long form is the standard; shortcuts are derived, not declared.
how.status_and_settings: CC's reading, not ruled: 'status' and 'settings' resolve through declared_views() so show/get/list already compose over them; `settings` is ALSO a bare verb (`cairn <device> settings`) that renders the settings view and says 'No settings' on an empty dict. The validate berth validate-20260906T111655-4ad94dfa32c8.json predates this ruling and covers only `list`; the build follows the ticket.
how.modifiers: Akien, 2026-09-06: `hot` — a modifier on show/get/list: "don't show cached values, get the real values." Verbatim: "lets say i type 'cairn librarian show status hot' ... 'hot' isn't in there yet. I added that just now. hot would mean don't show cached values, get the real values." A hot query requires the device to be running, so the shim's resolver starts the device (lazy init) before answering; without `hot`, the shim answers from what it holds (last_known / the cached view).

decisions.text: D-VOCABULARY. The vocabulary lives in the ROOT SHIM, not on Device: cairn/tools/base/shim.py declares ROOT_VERB_SEMANTICS, a module-level dict {verb: one-line meaning} in the ruled order list, show, get, stop, start, settings; ROOT_VERBS = tuple(ROOT_VERB_SEMANTICS) is DERIVED from it so the two cannot drift; ROOT_VIEWS = (status, settings) and HOT = hot stay as they are. There is no Device.VERBS and no handler name in the table — the handlers are the branches of BaseShim._resolve (ticket b41b0c0fff0e), which is the one resolver every device inherits; BaseDevice.declared_verbs (show, get) is the BUS menu and is untouched.
decisions.step: unlisted: declare root verb vocabulary as VERBS data structure

decisions.text: D-LIST. list already exists (b41b0c0fff0e) and this ticket only adds the semantics to it: its data is {verbs: [six], views: [status, settings, + device views], panes: [...], semantics: dict(ROOT_VERB_SEMANTICS)} and its text is the verbs:/views:/panes: blocks followed by a semantics: block with one line per verb 'verb: meaning'. Cold list reads views/panes from declared_contract(); hot from the device. Empty blocks print (none). No new handler is written.
decisions.step: unlisted: add list verb to enumerate verbs and views in JSON

decisions.text: D-COLLISION. The trigger point is REGISTRATION = the device waking: BaseShim._ensure_device calls the new staticmethod BaseShim._register(device) after _start_device and BEFORE setting _device/presence ONLINE/capturing a snapshot. _register raises RootVerbCollision(ValueError) when (a) a declared VIEW folds onto a root view — message exactly "device view 'status' collides with the root view" (same wording the b41b proof pins) — or (b) a declared BUS VERB folds onto a root verb and its handler is not the device's own _handle_<verb> method — message "device verb 'get' collides with the root verb — <meaning>; a device keeps the root meaning through _handle_get, never rebinds the word". Keeping or overriding _handle_show/_handle_get is legal; extending declared_verbs with **super() plus new verbs is legal; a device that wakes to None registers nothing. BaseShim.resolve catches RootVerbCollision as exit 2 with the message on stderr; the old resolve-time view-collision check is REMOVED (one mouth). deliver() reaches the same refusal through _ensure_device.
decisions.step: unlisted: refuse collision when a subclass re-declares a root verb (show/get/list/stop/start/settings)

decisions.text: D-PROCESS-MODEL. stop/start/settings are NOT re-implemented: start = BaseShim._ensure_device (in-process _start_device today; a real-process shim overrides), stop = BaseShim._stop_device (drops the instance, presence OFFLINE, snapshot kept), settings = the settings root view through _resolve rendering 'No settings' on an empty dict — all from b41b0c0fff0e, unchanged. Nothing is hoisted into Device.
decisions.step: unlisted: Hoist VERBS data structure into Device class

decisions.text: D-WIRING. No wiring change: the CLI dispatch already reads ROOT_VERBS (now derived from the table) and the bus dispatch (BaseShim.deliver) reads the device's declared_verbs(); the introspect menu is out of scope for this ticket — a device's introspect() carries intention/state/settings and the root vocabulary is answered by list, not by introspect.
decisions.step: unlisted: wire dispatch and introspect menu to read from VERBS

decisions.text: D-COLLISION-LOGIC. Detection is on the DICTS the device returns, at registration, in BaseShim._register(device) (shim.py 905-929): (a) for every key of device.declared_views(): canon(key, ROOT_VIEWS) folds the key through system_word and returns the root view it matches or None; a match raises RootVerbCollision('device view <root> collides with the root view'). (b) for every (verb, handler) in device.declared_verbs().items(): root = canon(verb, ROOT_VERBS); None → skip; else the collision is 'handler != getattr(device, "_handle_" + root, None)' — i.e. the VALUE bound to the root word must be the device's own bound method _handle_<root> (the base contract BaseDevice supplies for show/get); any other callable rebinds the word and raises RootVerbCollision('device verb <root> collides with the root verb — <meaning>; ...'). No runtime method lookup, no name-string comparison of handlers: it is dict keys folded by canon, and dict values compared by equality against the one permitted bound method. _register is called from _ensure_device at every wake; the shim catches RootVerbCollision at line 957 and exits 2 with the message on stderr, stdout empty, presence unchanged, no snapshot written.
decisions.step: D3 exact collision detection logic

decisions.text: D-RESPONSE-CONTRACT. Stated once, for every tooth: BaseShim.resolve(argv: list[str]) -> dict with exactly four keys — exit (int, 0 ok / 2 refused), text (str, the human rendering), data (the JSON half, dict or None), cached (bool, True when answered cold from the snapshot/contract). cli_main(shim_cls, argv) calls resolve, prints text to stdout, and exits with exit; --data mode in the proof's driver prints json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True) instead. Presence is the property shim.presence, one of the module constants NEVER_BOOTED / OFFLINE / ONLINE; it is read in-process right after resolve (the driver's --presence mode prints it). A snapshot is the file /home/akien/.cairn/devices/<device_id>/0/last_known.json, written only when a device wakes ONLINE; the proof lists them with home.rglob('last_known.json'). Subprocesses: the proof re-invokes ITSELF (sys.executable, __file__, '--drive', <which>, *argv) with HOME set to a scratch dir carrying a LIVE ground_loop liveness record, cwd=ROOT, PYTHONPATH=ROOT; <which> is a fixture name (view/verb/extender) or a roster device name.
decisions.step: D14 the shim response contract

decisions.text: D-HARNESS-LANDED. Nothing is replicated per test file and nothing is copied from test_root_verbs.py: the harness for THIS ticket is already written IN cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_root_verb_vocabulary.py (landed 8dd6cd81, amended 18e1923d) — fixture devices _Fixture/ViewCollider/VerbCollider/Extender and shims _FixtureShim/ViewColliderShim/VerbColliderShim/ExtenderShim, FIXTURES dict, _roster() (sorted names of cairn/devices/*/shim.py), _shim_class(name), _scratch() (mkdtemp + write_liveness), _run(home, which, *argv), _snapshots(home), the module-scoped home fixture, and _drive() with --register / --presence / --data modes. Terms: cold = the device is not running, answered from contract/snapshot; hot = argv carries 'hot', the device is woken and asked live; roster device = every directory under cairn/devices/ that has a shim.py (seven today); NEVER_BOOTED/OFFLINE/ONLINE = the three presence constants in shim.py. The builder's task for D6 is to run the file twice (pytest and python3 <file>), not to write it.
